summary: An excerpt from a novel (labeled Book 11, part 129) set at a graduation day in Riverboro. Rebecca is overwhelmed by the emotional aftermath of her success and receives sad news that Miss Sawyer, an invalid, is paralyzed though her speech is returning. Emma Jane offers to pack for her, while Adam Ladd and uncle Jerry Cobb talk about Rebecca's remarkable performance and voice.
one_line: At a Riverboro graduation, Rebecca feels the strain behind her triumph as news of Miss Sawyer's paralysis arrives and Adam Ladd and Mr. Cobb discuss her.
key_facts: Rebecca is told she can stay at the brick house and sleep, since Miss Sawyer's letter says she is better and Miranda has her speech back.
Emma Jane offers to pack Rebecca's trunk and attend to all their room things.
Rebecca sits in a quiet side pew with Hannah, Hannah's husband, and John.
Rebecca feels the day's honors have an air of unreality and that her condition is only transient.
Rebecca longs to steal away into the woods with John, who has grown so manly and handsome.
Uncle Jerry Cobb asks Adam Ladd whether girls like Rebecca are as thick as blackberries up in Boston.
Adam Ladd says Rebecca's voice made the others sound poor and thin.
Uncle Jerry says his mother scolds him for spoiling Rebecca, though his mother is not far behind in spoiling her.
Uncle Jerry says it made him sick to think of parents traveling miles to see their children graduate and then having to compare them with Rebecca.
Adam Ladd says he will drive Rebecca home the next day and offers to do so.
Uncle Jerry reports that the doctor does not know how serious Miss Sawyer's condition is.
Uncle Jerry says Miss Sawyer is paralyzed and will never walk again, but she has not lost her speech.
